transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I’m here because flying has just started to feel... way scarier than it should. Like, just the idea of getting on a plane makes me picture the turbulence we had on my honeymoon flight again. 

We went to Costa Rica for our honeymoon, actually, which was just so beautiful. The resort we stayed at had these wild iguanas that would just walk right up to the pool, and my husband was completely terrified of them. It’s funny because he's usually the brave one about that kind of stuff. I actually showed pictures of the iguanas to the kids at the preschool where I work—I'm an administrator there, so I mostly just deal with the parents and the scheduling, but I love popping into the classrooms when I can. The toddlers totally thought the lizards were dinosaurs, it was so cute. 

But, um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the flight. Yeah, so even though I know people fly safely every single day, just thinking about getting back in the air and feeling that dropping sensation again really freaks me out.
When did you first start feeling scared about flying?

Um, it started right after that turbulent flight back from our honeymoon. So that would be... gosh, about two years and five months ago now. We got married in October, which I just think is the absolute best time for a wedding because the weather is finally cooling down. My bridesmaids wore these gorgeous deep burgundy dresses, they looked so pretty. I actually still talk to all of them all the time, though my maid of honor, Jessica, just moved to Seattle for this big marketing job. She keeps begging me to come out and visit her, and I really want to because she says her new apartment has this amazing view of the water and she lives right by this famous farmer's market. But Seattle is just way too far to drive, and... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, so it's been about two years and five months since I started feeling this way.
Have you avoided any trips or travel plans because of your fear of flying?

Um, yeah, definitely. I’ve actually been choosing to take these really long drives instead of flying anywhere. Or I just turn down work trainings if they're out of state. Like, there was this one conference in Chicago last month that my boss really wanted me to go to. It was supposed to be all about new scheduling software for the preschool, which we desperately need because our current system is from, like, 2010 and it crashes every time two parents try to log in at the same time. The parents get so frustrated, and then they call me, and I have to spend half my morning just resetting passwords. One mom actually brought me a coffee the other day just to apologize for calling so much, which was really sweet, but she got me a dark roast and I’m definitely more of a blonde roast girl. I just think dark roast tastes kind of burnt, you know? 

But, um... oh, right, the travel plans. Yeah, so I didn't go to Chicago because I just couldn't handle the thought of the flight. And honestly, even if I just have to talk about planning a trip or looking at tickets, I absolutely need my husband sitting right there with me to get through it, otherwise I'll just panic and back out completely.
Have you avoided any social events or gatherings because your friends or family wanted to meet at a location that would require you to fly to get there?

Um, well, mostly I've just been pushing back personal plans. Like, my husband and I had been saving up and planning this big trip to Florence. I've always wanted to go to Italy, especially for the food. I took this pasta-making class locally a few months ago—well, my sister dragged me to it for her birthday. We made ravioli from scratch, and it was so messy, there was flour literally everywhere. My sister somehow managed to get it all over her black sweater, which was hilarious, but the ravioli actually turned out amazing. We filled it with this butternut squash and sage ricotta mixture that the instructor showed us how to make. The instructor was actually from Naples originally, and she had the thickest accent. She kept telling us that Americans cook their pasta way too long, which I guess is true because hers was perfectly al dente. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, social things and flying. Yeah, so the Florence trip keeps getting pushed back because I just can't bring myself to book the flights. I’m still managing my job and home life fine, you know, getting through the day-to-day stuff. But it's definitely affecting things. Like I mentioned earlier, I’ve started passing up those out-of-state trainings and conferences that my supervisor really thinks would help me grow in my role at the preschool. It's just... I can't do the plane ride.
Do you experience anxiety or fear in situations other than flying?

Um, no, not really. It's pretty much just the flying. I mean, I don't love spiders, but who does, right? We actually had this huge spider in the preschool playground last week, right by the sandbox. The kids were completely fascinated by it, of course, but I was just trying to herd them away without making a big deal out of it. Little Tommy—he's in the four-year-old room—he kept trying to poke it with a stick, and I had to physically pick him up and move him. He's going through this phase where he just wants to poke everything. Last Tuesday he poked a hole right through his juice box at snack time, and it got all over the rug. We have these really nice, brightly colored alphabet rugs, and grape juice just does not come out, no matter what you use. Our janitor, Mr. Henderson, tried three different cleaners, and now it just smells like grape juice and bleach in there. 

But, um... oh, right, other things. No, I'm generally pretty calm about everything else. I don't get scared driving or being in crowds or anything like that. It's literally just the airplanes.
Has your fear of flying caused any problems or tension in your relationships with family or friends?

Um, well, I wouldn't say it's caused like, major problems or anything. My husband is really understanding about it, mostly. He knows how much I want to go to Italy, and he's just kind of waiting until I'm ready. He's actually been spending a lot of time lately looking at different train routes we could take if we ever get over there, which is sweet. He loves trains. We actually took this scenic train ride up through the mountains for our anniversary a couple of years ago, the one that goes through all those old mining towns? It was beautiful, especially the leaves turning colors, but they served this lunch on board that was just... questionable. It was supposed to be chicken salad, but it had these weird chunks of celery that were way too big, and it was so heavy on the mayonnaise. I ended up just eating the little packet of crackers it came with. I'm kind of picky about chicken salad anyway, like, I think it needs a little bit of dill, maybe some dried cranberries if you want to get fancy. My mom makes the best chicken salad, she always puts toasted pecans in hers. 

But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, relationships! Yeah, no, my friends and family are pretty cool about it. They know I don't fly right now, so if we do a girls' weekend or something, we just pick somewhere we can drive to. So, no, no real tension or anything like that.
On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate your level of anxiety when you think about flying?

Um, well, on a scale of 1 to 10... I guess it kind of depends, but it's pretty high. Like, if I'm just looking at flights for one of those conferences online, or even if I'm just outside and hear a plane flying overhead, my chest gets all tight right away. I get this sudden rush of panic, like I just need to slam my laptop shut or completely get away from the thought of it. It's almost like a reflex. Speaking of laptops, I actually need to take mine in to get looked at. The 'E' key has been sticking for like two weeks now. I think it’s because my cat, Barnaby, knocked over a mug of green tea near it. He’s a Maine Coon mix, so he’s huge and just so clumsy. He doesn't even realize how big he is. Yesterday he tried to jump onto the windowsill in the kitchen and completely missed, taking down my favorite little succulent plant with him. Dirt went absolutely everywhere, and of course, it was right after I had just swept the floor. I swear, he waits until I clean to make a mess. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, the scale! Yeah, so I'd say the anxiety is probably like a... maybe an 8 or a 9 when I actually have to think about it or look at flights. It just hits me really fast.
Are there any parts of your daily routine or responsibilities that you've had to change or avoid because of your fear of flying?

Um, yeah, I guess I have changed a few things. Like, I’ve been choosing long drives instead of flying for vacations, or I'll just turn down work trainings if they're out of state. My boss actually wanted me to go to this early childhood development seminar in Chicago next month, and I had to make up an excuse about my sister coming to visit. Which, she actually is coming to visit, but not until November. She lives in Oregon, and it's always such a big deal when she comes because she brings her two dogs. They're these little terrier mixes, super high energy. Last time they were here, they completely tore up one of my couch pillows. Just fluff everywhere. I was finding stuffing in the living room for like a month, even after vacuuming a dozen times. My vacuum is actually starting to make this weird whining noise, I think the belt might be going out. I bought it at a garage sale like five years ago, so I guess it's had a good run, but they're just so expensive to replace now. 

But, um... oh, right, the routine stuff. Yeah, so I avoid flying whenever possible. And if I absolutely have to even just talk about planning a trip or looking at flights, I need my husband sitting right there with me to help me get through it, otherwise I'll just panic and back out completely.
Have you felt that your fear of flying has impacted your ability to perform your job duties effectively?

Um, effectively? I mean, I guess I'm still managing my job and everything at home okay. It's not like I'm getting fired or anything. But, well, like I mentioned with that Chicago seminar, I've started passing up a lot of those trainings and conferences. My supervisor keeps suggesting them because she thinks they'd really help me grow and, you know, maybe move up to a director position eventually. She's really big on professional development. She actually just finished her master's degree online, which I think is amazing because she has three kids under the age of ten. I don't know how she does it. Her youngest, Liam, is in one of our preschool classrooms, and he is just a little tornado. The other day he decided to paint his own shoes during art time. Just completely covered his brand new light-up sneakers in bright blue tempera paint. His mom was surprisingly chill about it, though. She said she's just going to call them his "custom kicks." I wish I was that laid back. I get stressed out just trying to figure out what to make for dinner most nights. 

But, um... wait, job duties, right. Yeah, so I'm doing my day-to-day stuff fine, but it's definitely holding me back from growing in my career. And it's just really frustrating because it keeps pushing back my personal plans, too, like that trip to Florence I've been so excited about. It just feels like everything is on hold.
Are there any other areas of your life, besides travel, where you feel your fear of flying is having an impact?

Other areas of my life? Um... I don't really think so. It's pretty much just the flying and the travel stuff. I mean, my day-to-day life here on the ground is totally fine. Actually, we just started this big community garden project at the preschool, which has been taking up so much of my free time anyway, so I haven't even had time to think about much else. We got these massive raised beds donated by a local hardware store. The delivery guy was so nice, he actually helped us carry them all the way around to the back playground. Though, he accidentally stepped on one of the plastic toy trucks and completely shattered it. It was one of those really sturdy-looking yellow dump trucks, too. The kids were a little upset, but we distracted them with the dirt. You should have seen them, they were covered in potting soil within five minutes. We're trying to grow cherry tomatoes and zucchini, but honestly, I don't have a green thumb at all. Last year I managed to kill a cactus. A cactus! You're barely even supposed to water them. My husband says I love plants to death because I always overwater them. He's the one who usually takes care of the yard and the landscaping... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, if the flying thing affects anything else. But yeah, no, besides the trips and missing out on those out-of-state conferences, it really doesn't bother me in my normal everyday routine.
Are there any friends or family members that you've become distant from because of your inability to fly to visit them?

Um, no, not really. I mean, my sister in Oregon is probably the farthest one away, and we still talk on the phone all the time. She's actually the one who usually comes out here anyway because of her dogs. I told you about the dogs, right? The little terrier mixes? Yeah, they are just a handful. But honestly, most of my family is pretty local. My parents are just a couple of hours away, and my husband's family is all in the same state, so we just drive for holidays. 

Actually, Thanksgiving is going to be at his parents' house this year, and I'm already kind of stressing about it because his mom always makes this sweet potato casserole with the marshmallows on top, and it is just... way too sweet. I tried to bring a different side dish last year—this really nice Brussels sprouts thing with bacon and balsamic glaze—and I think she was a little offended. She barely even touched it. And then my husband's brother, who is super into fitness right now, started lecturing everyone about the sugar content in the marshmallows. He just started doing CrossFit, and it's literally all he talks about. He was trying to get my husband to go with him to this 5 AM class, and I was just thinking, there is no way we are waking up that early...

But, um... sorry, what was the question? Oh, distant from family. Yeah, no, everyone's mostly close by, so the flying thing doesn't really get in the way of seeing them.
Do you feel like your fear of flying has changed the way you interact with your loved ones?

Changed the way I interact with them? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, they know I don't like flying, so it's not like it's a secret or anything. My husband is super supportive about it, even though he loves to travel. We actually just celebrated our anniversary last weekend, and instead of going anywhere crazy, we just did a staycation. We went to this new Italian place downtown—the one that took over the old bank building? Oh my gosh, the architecture inside is gorgeous. They kept the original vault doors and everything. We had this amazing truffle risotto, but the waiter was so strange. He kept hovering right behind my husband's chair. Like, uncomfortably close. My husband is too polite to say anything, but I could tell he was getting annoyed. He gets this little twitch by his eye when he's irritated. He's had that since we started dating. We met at a coffee shop, actually, and he spilled his Americano all over my laptop bag...

Wait, sorry. The flying thing. Yeah, no, it hasn't really changed how I interact with anyone. They just know it's a thing I struggle with, and we just kind of work around it.

Though, he accidentally stepped on one of the plastic toy trucks and completely shattered it. It was one of those really sturdy-looking yellow dump trucks, too. The kids were a little upset, but we distracted them with the dirt. You should have seen them, they were covered in potting soil within five minutes. We're trying to grow cherry tomatoes and zucchini, but honestly, I don't have a green thumb at all. Last year I managed to kill a cactus. A cactus! You're barely even supposed to water them. My husband says I love plants to death because I always overwater them. He's the one who usually takes care of the yard and the landscaping... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, if the flying thing affects anything else. But yeah, no, besides the trips and missing out on those out-of-state conferences, it really doesn't bother me in my normal everyday routine.

patient.answer:
Um, no, not really. I mean, my sister in Oregon is probably the farthest one away, and we still talk on the phone all the time. She's actually the one who usually comes out here anyway because of her dogs. I told you about the dogs, right? The little terrier mixes? Yeah, they are just a handful. But honestly, most of my family is pretty local. My parents are just a couple of hours away, and my husband's family is all in the same state, so we just drive for holidays. 

Actually, Thanksgiving is going to be at his parents' house this year, and I'm already kind of stressing about it because his mom always makes this sweet potato casserole with the marshmallows on top, and it is just... way too sweet. I tried to bring a different side dish last year—this really nice Brussels sprouts thing with bacon and balsamic glaze—and I think she was a little offended. She barely even touched it. And then my husband's brother, who is super into fitness right now, started lecturing everyone about the sugar content in the marshmallows. He just started doing CrossFit, and it's literally all he talks about. He was trying to get my husband to go with him to this 5 AM class, and I was just thinking, there is no way we are waking up that early...

But, um... sorry, what was the question? Oh, distant from family. Yeah, no, everyone's mostly close by, so the flying thing doesn't really get in the way of seeing them.

patient.answer:
Changed the way I interact with them? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, they know I don't like flying, so it's not like it's a secret or anything. My husband is super supportive about it, even though he loves to travel. We actually just celebrated our anniversary last weekend, and instead of going anywhere crazy, we just did a staycation. We went to this new Italian place downtown—the one that took over the old bank building? Oh my gosh, the architecture inside is gorgeous. They kept the original vault doors and everything. We had this amazing truffle risotto, but the waiter was so strange. He kept hovering right behind my husband's chair. Like, uncomfortably close. My husband is too polite to say anything, but I could tell he was getting annoyed. He gets this little twitch by his eye when he's irritated. He's had that since we started dating. We met at a coffee shop, actually, and he spilled his Americano all over my laptop bag...

Wait, sorry. The flying thing. Yeah, no, it hasn't really changed how I interact with anyone. They just know it's a thing I struggle with, and we just kind of work around it.
